scenes.headline: How open models confer before they answer
scenes.sub: Mixture-of-Agents, and how Nous Research ran it on Hermes.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pickle! Mixture-of-Agents lets several open models read each other's drafts before one answer goes out. Here's how it works.

scenes.label: Collaborativeness
scenes.text: An LLM writes a better answer when it is shown other models' responses, even responses weaker than what it would have written alone.
scenes.say: The idea: a model writes a better answer when it reads other models' drafts, even drafts weaker than its own. The paper calls it collaborativeness.

steps.say: The prompt goes to several proposers, deliberately different models. You want different mistakes, not the same answer four times.
Every draft, plus the query, goes into an aggregate-and-synthesize prompt: critically evaluate these, and fuse them.

steps.note: the paper's default: 3 layers of 6 proposers
steps.say: Every agent in the next layer reads all of the last layer's outputs, and writes again.
The final aggregator emits the answer. It isn't voting, it's reading: keeping the part each proposer got right.

scenes.title: Forge, on Hermes 70B
scenes.say: Nous Research shipped this in its Forge Reasoning API, on top of Hermes seventy B, alongside two other techniques.

items.say: Mixture-of-Agents for breadth: propose, confer, synthesize.
Tree search for depth: more thinking on promising branches.
And Chain of Code for grounding: run the arithmetic instead of bluffing it.

scenes.title: The textbook stack, and a cheap one

left.title: The textbook stack
items: Layers of proposers, then an aggregator
left.say: The textbook stack costs many model calls per answer, and latency grows with every layer.

right.title: One layer, two roles
items: A small reference model drafts first
Its draft rides along as private context
The Hermes agent aggregates and calls tools
right.say: A cheap version: a small reference model drafts first, and the Hermes agent aggregates it while running its own tool calls.

scenes.title: AlpacaEval 2.0 win rate
scenes.say: In the paper, open models conferring scored sixty-five point one percent, against fifty-seven point five for GPT-4 Omni on its own.

scenes.text: Diversity beats raw strength: proposers that fail differently give the aggregator more to fuse than copies of the best model.

recap: Proposers draft; aggregators read every draft and fuse
Even weaker drafts make a model answer better
Nous ran it on Hermes in Forge
scenes.say: To recap: diverse drafts, read and fused, layer by layer. And Nous ran it on Hermes.
